component.name: MimirDLP
component.summary: Download videos and music with yt-dlp

description.p: A graphical front end for yt-dlp. Paste a link and it looks the video up before anything is downloaded, showing the title, thumbnail and length (for a playlist, its name and how many videos it has). Then pick video or audio, the format and the quality.

Several links can be queued at once, each with its own format and progress bar. They run one after another. A failed download can be retried, a stopped one resumes from the partial file, and whatever was still waiting is back the next time you open the app.

ul.li: Subtitles (including the automatic ones), thumbnails, metadata and chapters, embedded or kept
SponsorBlock: mark sponsor segments as chapters, or cut them out of the file (YouTube only)
Playlists: the whole list, one video from it, or a range
A history file, to skip what you already downloaded
Audio extraction, container conversion, speed limit and file name templates
Light and dark themes; English and Spanish, with translations on Weblate

description.p: The package includes yt-dlp, FFmpeg and Deno, so nothing is downloaded when the app starts. The yt-dlp in it is the stable release and only gets newer when the package does. Signing in with your browser's cookies doesn't work inside the sandbox yet.
Use it within the law and each site's terms; you are responsible for what you download.

ul.li: On Windows the app uses much less memory: the window is drawn with DirectX 12 instead of Vulkan.
On Windows the window opens in about half a second instead of one and a half.
A setting to draw the window with the processor instead of the graphics card, for computers whose graphics card gives trouble.
On Windows, "Show in folder" now selects the file when its path has spaces, instead of opening Documents.
Closing the app no longer leaves a white rectangle behind for a moment on Windows.
A settings file saved with a byte order mark no longer loses its first setting.
A redesigned interface: icons, the link field in the header bar, clearer download cards with their status at a glance, and the same layout on every screen, in both themes.
A welcome on the first launch, with one progress bar while the tools are installed.
Settings rows line up, with switches on the right.
Opens faster: the tools are no longer started on every launch to check their version.
On Windows, no more white window for a moment while the app opens.
When a download fails for a common reason, the card says what happened and what to do, such as signing in or waiting after too many requests.
Stopping a live stream saves what was recorded so far.
A password for videos a site protects with one, never saved to disk.
A choice between nightly and stable yt-dlp builds, and a setting for retries after network errors.
A notice when a new version of MimirDLP is out, and a button that copies diagnostic information for bug reports.
The activity log no longer shows your IP address, and the libraries the app is built on are updated with security fixes.

description.p: Remembers the size of the window between launches.
Corrects the description of what the package includes, and no longer repeats the title in the Download header bar.
Ready to run as a Flatpak, with yt-dlp, FFmpeg and Deno included in the package. Clearer wording in Spanish.
Installed somewhere it can't write to, MimirDLP keeps its files in your user folder and saves to your Downloads folder. Settings now survive updates through Scoop.
A link you copy now shows up in the box when you switch to MimirDLP, ready to add.
